title: LANTERN-XGB predicts occult lymph node metastasis in early lung cancer
summary: LANTERN-XGB, an XGBoost workflow with SHAP-based selection on CT, PET and clinical features, was developed in 437 patients with clinical N0 NSCLC and validated on prospective (n=100) and independent external (n=100) datasets. External AUC was about 0.77, comparable to nomogram benchmarks. Performance is modest, and the abstract does not establish clinical benefit.
ai_technology: XGBoost multi-stage workflow with SHAP-based hierarchical feature selection on multimodal data
organization: Dresden University of Technology, University Hospital Carl Gustav Carus; Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf

evidence.tested: Validation on a prospective dataset and an independent external dataset.
evidence.unknown: It is not stated that the model was frozen before the prospective set, and impact on decisions is not established; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicted occult lymph node metastasis from multimodal features.
